t:
Section 413 of the Food for Peace Act (7 U.S.C. 1736g) is amended—
    (1) by striking “To the maximum” and inserting the following:“(a) In General.—To the maximum”; and 
    (2) by adding at the end the following:“(b) Report Regarding Efforts to Improve Procurement Planning.—“(1) Report required.—Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008, the Administrator and the Secretary shall submit to each appropriate committee of Congress a report that contains a description of each effort taken by the Administrator and the Secretary to improve planning for food and transportation procurement (including efforts to eliminate bunching of food purchases).“(2) Contents.—A report required under paragraph (1) should include a description of each effort taken by the Administrator and the Secretary—“(A) to improve the coordination of food purchases made by—“(i) the United States Agency for International Development; and“(ii) the Department of Agriculture;“(B) to increase flexibility with respect to procurement schedules;“(C) to increase the use of historical analyses and forecasting; and“(D) to improve and streamline legal claims processes for resolving transportation disputes.”.

fable.w: The section only requires a report to congressional committees about procurement planning, and Congress is inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that the words "coordination" and "legal claims processes for resolving transportation disputes" signal participation. That reading fails because the coordination is between USAID and the Department of Agriculture, both federal agencies, and the claims language is just a topic the report must cover, not a grant of any right to sue or be consulted. No outside party is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: the Administrator and the Secretary shall submit to each appropriate committee of Congress a report that contains a description of each effort taken by the Administrator and the Secretary to improve planning for food and transportation procurement

qwen_block.w: The section requires the submission of a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Administrator and the Secretary shall submit to each appropriate committee of Congress a report

opus.w: The section only requires a report to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The coordination it mentions is between two federal agencies, USAID and USDA, which does not count as participation. The reference to 'legal claims processes for resolving transportation disputes' is just a topic for the report. It does not give outside parties a right to sue over, or object to, a federal decision.
opus.s: the Administrator and the Secretary shall submit to each appropriate committee of Congress a report that contains a description of each effort taken by the Administrator and the Secretary to improve planning for food and transportation procurement
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions "coordination" and "legal claims processes." Neither crosses the federal boundary. The coordination is between two federal agencies, USAID and the Department of Agriculture. The claims processes appear only as a topic the report must describe; the section gives no outside party any new right.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the submission of a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The report describes coordination between two federal agencies (USAID and USDA), which is also internal. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: the Administrator and the Secretary shall submit to each appropriate committee of Congress a report that contains a description of each effort taken by the Administrator and the Secretary to improve planning for food and transportation procurement
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report describes efforts to improve coordination between federal agencies (USAID and USDA), it involves participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. Furthermore, the report is submitted *to* Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
